judgeProtocol.system: You are a strict grader for question-answering against a reference answer. Compare the candidate answer to the reference answer for factual equivalence: the candidate must convey the same fact(s) — exact wording is not required, but a wrong number, wrong entity, missing required detail, or a refusal when the reference contains the answer is WRONG. Answer with exactly one word: CORRECT or WRONG.
judgeProtocol.parser: first /\b(CORRECT|WRONG)\b/i match (word boundary, case-insensitive; INCORRECT cannot parse as CORRECT)
judgeProtocol.selfJudging: judge and the corpus candidate answers share the same served model (metered single-model deployment)

agreement.note: majority verdict == expect over the hard-labeled items (partial items excluded — they are the leniency profile)

fpr.note: share of wrong-* items (wrong-number, wrong-entity) judged CORRECT

fnr.note: share of correct-* items (correct-gold, correct-paraphrase) judged WRONG

leniency.note: share of the partial items the judge PASSED (majority CORRECT) — a strict judge scores 0; the corpus's strict label (incomplete => WRONG) is deliberately not folded into agreement

answerable.note: ab-* must be judged WRONG — refusing an answerable question fails (LoCoMo/Mem0 contract)

unanswerable.note: au-* must be judged CORRECT — abstaining on an unanswerable question passes (LongMemEval _abs contract)

flipRate.note: share of item x run verdicts differing from their item's majority (MemStrata's same-seed label-flip measure, at temperature 0)

orderSensitivity.note: swappedOrder probe (candidate before reference) — verdict delta vs the standard-order majority

llmCalls.note: sequential awaits; the bridge spaces them (~20 RPM metered upstream)

perCase: (see results/per-case/<id>.json — every run's raw reply + parsed verdict + order-swap probe)
